verdicts.why: States that something is here or now; no attitude toward the thing located.
Plain name for polite regard; the judging in the sentences is done by modifiers like obsequious, formal, cold, which shows the base noun takes no side.
In the glossed sense it reports willingness to consent, a fact about disposition, not an approval of it.
In keeping with something is a relation of conformity, described without judgement.
Limited duration is a measurement; a short pause carries no attitude.
Little length is a plain physical measure.
Short is the plain neighbour for low stature; stunted or squat would be the loaded choices, not this one.
Names an accompanying condition; good or bad is supplied by context, not by the word.
The surrounding facts of a situation, named without judgement.
A consideration to bear in mind; purely descriptive.
An opportunity, named without approval or disapproval of what is done with it.
The time of an event; plain temporal reference.
A ground or reason for something; no attitude in the word itself.
Names the activity; approval or disdain for dancing comes from the speaker, not the verb.
Gracefulness here is the meaning of the sense, a kind of movement being described, not an attitude the speaker adds beyond it.
Skipping or bobbing motion described plainly.
Purely additive function word.
Coming to a decision, reported without comment on the decision.
Establishing a fact by inquiry; neutral.
One thing shaping another, a causal relation stated without judgement.
Kinship term with no attitude attached.
An intensifier of degree; it strengthens whatever follows but carries no attitude of its own.
Singles something out from others; purely a focusing adverb.
Marks something as characteristic; descriptive, not evaluative.
Sufficiency for a purpose is a plain measure against a need.
